record.original_question: Is every question guaranteed to have at least one answer, and conversely is every assertion necessarily the result of at least one question?

evidence.quote: Mathematical Logic: Is it true that for any question there is at least an answer? Reciprocally: Is any assertion the result of at least a question?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a formal framework in which one distinguishes two kinds of well-formed expressions: questions and assertions. Assume there is a relation "A is an answer to Q" between assertions A and questions Q, and a relation "A is the result of Q" expressing that the assertion A is obtained as the outcome of posing the question Q. Within such a framework, decide the following two statements:

(a) For every question Q, there exists at least one assertion A such that A is an answer to Q.

(b) Conversely, for every assertion A, there exists at least one question Q such that A is the result of Q.

Determine under what natural axiomatizations of the logic of questions and assertions both (a) and (b) hold, and whether either can fail in a reasonable formal system.
artifact.status_search_result: The question, phrased as a foundational/philosophical query about the logic of questions and assertions (erotetic logic), is open-ended and not formulated as a precise theorem with a definite truth value. No specific resolution in the literature was identified; the status is best described as unknown/ill-posed without a fixed formal framework.
